Saudi Steel Pipe Co Reports Steady Financial Performance for First Quarter

Dammam – Saudi Steel Pipe Co, a leading manufacturer in the Kingdom’s steel sector, announced its financial results for the first quarter of 2024, showing steady revenues and reaffirming its role in supporting the region’s construction and energy industries. The company reported total revenues of SAR 175 million for the quarter ending March 31, an increase of 3.5% over the same period last year. Net profit stood at SAR 11.2 million, compared to SAR 10.7 million in the first quarter of 2023.

Company officials attributed the positive results to stable demand from oil, gas, and infrastructure projects across the Eastern Province and beyond. “We have continued to see healthy order flows from key sectors, particularly in energy and water transmission. Our focus on operational efficiency and product quality is delivering consistent results,” said Eng. Fahad Al-Qahtani, CEO of Saudi Steel Pipe Co, in a statement accompanying the financials.

The company’s board approved a dividend of SAR 0.10 per share for shareholders of record as of May 10. “This dividend reflects our ongoing commitment to rewarding our investors while maintaining a robust balance sheet,” said Al-Qahtani.

Industry analysts noted that the steel sector has benefited from sustained government investment in infrastructure, especially under the Vision 2030 initiative. “Steel pipe manufacturers in the Kingdom continue to benefit from a steady pipeline of projects. Saudi Steel Pipe Co’s results are in line with sector expectations,” commented Ahmed Al-Mansour, an analyst at Eastern Markets Advisory.

The company continues to invest in workforce development and production technology. According to a spokesperson, recent upgrades at its Dammam facility have improved production efficiency and reduced energy consumption.

The National Steel Workers’ Union welcomed the results, citing stable employment levels at the plant. “Our members appreciate the company’s commitment to steady operations and investment in training programs,” said union representative Saleh Al-Dosari.

Saudi Steel Pipe Co is expected to maintain its current production levels for the coming quarter, with management expressing cautious optimism about continued demand from regional infrastructure projects and energy developments.
